newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam to offer T-notes, rate target 11.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam to offer T-notes, rate target 11.5 pct.

text.p: Vietnam will offer 50 billion dong ($4.46 million) of Treasury notes at an auction on Wednesday, an official at the central State Bank said on Tuesday.
He said the Ministry of Finance had set a target annual yield of 11.50 percent for paper sold at the auction.

At last week's sale, the first of the year, the government sold 10 billion dong of one-year notes to a single bidder, state-owned Vietcombank, at a rate of 10.99 percent. It had originally offered 30 billion dong worth of notes and targeted a rate of 11 percent for that sale.
The State Bank official said the newly adopted target rate for auctions was not a ceiling. In theory, bidders over the target rate receive allocations until the total amount on offer is allotted.

Analysts say foreign and domestic institutions' interest in Treasury auctions collapsed last year because the government capped interest rates and also withdrew tax exemption on interest income from Treasury paper. ($1 = 11,200 dong)
